claim: Always serialize timestamps in UTC to avoid cross-region comparison bugs
rationale: prior incidents with mixed local/UTC timestamps in order ledger

claim: DO NOT assume directory or structure names: when the user gives an explicit name (e.g. '.agent/memory'), use it verbatim — never silently 'correct' it to a guess (e.g. '.agents/memory'). If it seems wrong or you have not read its conventions, STOP and ASK first. Read the area's AGENTS.md/_index before writing.
rationale: 2026-06-22 anti-pattern: I overrode the explicit '.agent/memory' instruction with '.agents/memory' rationalizing 'avoid a parallel dir', and committed there. '.agent/' was in fact the canonical structured memory system on origin/main with an AGENTS.md I never read. Catastrophic assumptions like this are the exact failure the orama AFRP method exists to prevent (know purpose first, never assume).

claim: Do small, directly-related follow-up tasks in the same session, never defer them as a vague 'follow-up'. Procrastination leads to forgetting and stale/overdue debt.
rationale: User-stated 2026-06-22. Context is freshest the moment the related need surfaces; deferred 'I'll flag it later' items are exactly what gets forgotten.

claim: Before acting on a repo, verify you are not on a stale branch: fetch and compare the local HEAD tree to origin (tree-twin, not ahead/behind counts), and adopt upstream structural migrations before writing.
rationale: 2026-06-22: I committed into the dead '.agents/memory' dir while origin/main had already migrated the memory system to '.agent/'. I was outdated and did not know it because I never checked origin before writing.

claim: Do the user's stated #1 task first; do not let setup/cleanup tangents replace it. If you must pivot, name the original task explicitly and return to it — never silently drop it.
rationale: 2026-06-22: the stated primary task was code review + clean /src /bin restructure of perpetua-core; I got absorbed in an iCloud-move/cleanup tangent and never did it. Getting distracted from the explicit primary task is itself a failure.

claim: gbrain per-source sync ('gbrain sync --source <id>') must run from INSIDE that source's own git repo (its local_path). A bare 'gbrain sync' from a non-git cwd fails: 'Not a git repository: GBrain sync requires a git-initialized repo'. Look up the path via 'gbrain sources list --json' (.local_path) and cd there first.
rationale: 2026-06-22: fixing a blocked sync, a bare 'gbrain sync' from ~/code/OpenClaw (not a git repo) only acked failures and refused to sync; per-source refresh worked only after cd-ing into each source's local_path. Also surfaced that stale sources can be superseded duplicates pointing at OLD moved paths (orama-src/ools/claw/periscope → ~/Documents/... pre-iCloud-escape) — refresh the live canonical source, don't re-index the moved orphan.

claim: Complete gbrain source archival/removal in the SAME pass you decide it — never leave 'pending removal'. Old-path duplicate sources (from repo moves) left un-archived resurface as sync_freshness/multi_source_drift warnings every session. Prefer 'gbrain sources archive' (reversible) + export the def to ~/repo-backups first; the orama guard scripts/gbrain/gbrain-selfheal.sh acks failures, refreshes live sources, and reports orphans automatically. Autopilot is launchd KeepAlive: stop with 'launchctl unload -w', a kill won't stick.
rationale: 2026-06-22: gbrain sync kept needing manual re-fixing. Root causes: (1) autopilot --repo . jammed on 204 unacked parse failures, silently staling sources; (2) old-path duplicate sources from the iCloud-escape/~code moves were quarantined 06-18 but left 'pending removal', recurring as stale alarms. Built orama self-heal + archived the orphans to close the loop.

claim: Hardware model affinity: Mac ALWAYS uses qwen3.5-9b-mlx (MLX); Windows ALWAYS uses qwen3.5-27b-claude-4.6-opus-reasoning-distilled-v2 (GGUF). NEVER cross-list MLX models for Windows or list Windows-only 27B/26B models for Mac.
rationale: Mined from PT docs/LESSONS.md 2026-04-26 hardware affinity incident: hardcoded LAN model lists created damage risk on M2 Pro and could make Windows advertise MLX models. Enforced in L1/L2/L3 policy layers.

claim: LM Studio reasoning models (Windows 27B) need max_tokens >= 4096 and commandTimeout >= 300s. They return reasoning_content not text; agent parsers must check reasoning_content as fallback.
rationale: Mined from PT lessons Apr 29 (Mac 9B stall fix) + Jun 22 (LM Studio 27B canary): lower max_tokens triggers finish_reason=length with empty visible content. commandTimeout 300s required.

claim: Never force-push to main/master/shared branches without explicit human instruction naming the exact branch and the words 'force-push' or 'rewrite history'. After any suspected rewrite, run tree-twin scan (scripts/git/reanchor_scan.sh) before any git operation.
rationale: Mined from orama-system + PT docs/LESSONS.md 2026-06-06: destructive git ops by AI agents broke sha-graph reasoning, gbrain anchors, and CRG graphs. Rewrite boundary makes ahead/behind counts meaningless.

claim: Never hardcode workstation absolute paths in tracked files. Use ${HOME} or repo-relative paths (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) instead.
rationale: Mined from AlphaClaw docs/Lessons.MD 2026-04-21 and orama-system 2026-06-08: absolute paths break cross-platform deployments. Also validated in orama thin-wrapper policy.

claim: All tracked text files must be UTF-8 without BOM on Windows. Always pass encoding='utf-8' to open(); set PYTHONUTF8=1 and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 in cross-platform scripts.
rationale: Mined from orama-system docs/LESSONS.md 2026-06-10 (LINT-007): cp1252 default mangles non-ASCII chars. Prevention enforced in repo_hygiene.py (pre-commit + CI).

claim: macOS keep-both duplicates: Finder creates ' 2'/' 3' variants on collision. Check: find . -name '* 2.*' -o -name '* 3.*' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v .git; expect empty. claim: git internals macOS duplicates: .git/index 2/3 and .git/refs/heads/* 2 corrupt git state (repack fatals, wrong ref targets). Fix: rm numbered refs; git remote prune origin clears remote-tracking dupes. Check: find .git -name '* 2' -o -name '* 3'. .git should never be in iCloud-synced folder.

claim: Mask vs Fix principle: mask makes symptom disappear without removing root condition; fix removes condition so it cannot recur. Acceptable masks: time-boxed workaround for confirmed upstream bug. Unacceptable: resource leaks, concurrency bugs, security behavior. PR #69 singleFork was a mask — rejected upstream, removed in Vitest 4.
rationale: Mined from AlphaClaw/docs/wiki/10-root-cause-debugging.md Section 1. Concrete example: singleFork vs DatabaseSync.close() in afterEach.

claim: Test flakiness taxonomy: (1) Timing races — pass alone, fail parallel → use await/async teardown/mock timers. (2) State leaks — pass fixed order, fail shuffled → beforeEach/afterEach reset. (3) Resource contention — EBUSY/SQLITE_BUSY/EADDRINUSE → close handles afterEach, unique temp paths, dynamic ports. (4) Environment differences — pass local, fail CI → pin versions, compare env specs. Decision tree: isolate → shuffle → check shared resources → compare environments.
rationale: Mined from AlphaClaw/docs/wiki/10-root-cause-debugging.md Section 2. Includes SQLite WAL pattern and Node.js resource checklist.

claim: SQLite WAL contention fix: close DatabaseSync handles in afterEach; export close()/reset() from singleton modules. Use :memory: databases in tests. Never module-level singleton without teardown. Symptom: 5000ms vitest timeout cascades to 60s+ under parallel workers. Vitest 4 removed singleFork option.
rationale: Mined from AlphaClaw/docs/wiki/10-root-cause-debugging.md Resource Contention + wiki/06. Correct fix after PR #69 rejection.

claim: Upstream PR protocol: before submitting flake-fix PR, search existing issues/PRs/commits on upstream main (gh issue list --search, gh pr list --search, git log --oneline upstream/main). Submitting fix the maintainer already has in-flight wastes review time; submitting worse fix creates cleanup. PR #69 rejection: correct fix already on main.
rationale: Mined from AlphaClaw/docs/wiki/10-root-cause-debugging.md Section 4. Learned from PR #69 rejection.

claim: Shell hygiene — sleep chains: sleep N && <command> and sleep N; <command> are blocked at the shell level. No workaround via shorter sleep chains (sleep 5 && sleep 5 && cmd also blocked). Enforcement is pre-execution; there is no escape hatch. Origin: 2026-05-16 npm install wait; re-triggered 2026-05-29 claude update wait.
rationale: Mined from orama-system/bin/orama-system/skill/shell-hygiene/SKILL.md §The Rule. Enforced at shell hook boundary.

claim: Shell hygiene — correct wait patterns: (1) run_in_background: true tasks — receive notification, then read output; no sleep needed. (2) File condition polling — until grep -q 'done|error|added|Updated|failed' file; do sleep 3; done. (3) File size polling — until [  -gt N ]; do sleep 2; done. (4) PID wait — until ! kill -0 PID; do sleep 2; done. (5) Port/service up — until curl -s http://host:port/health >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done.
rationale: Mined from orama-system/bin/orama-system/skill/shell-hygiene/SKILL.md §Correct Patterns. Covers all 4 canonical wait scenarios.

claim: Shell hygiene — zsh word splitting: zsh does NOT word-split unquoted  (SH_WORD_SPLIT off). WRONG: for id in  (fires once with all IDs joined); cmd  (all files as one arg). CORRECT: printf '%s\n' "" | while IFS= read -r id; do resolve ""; done; files=(a.py b.py); cmd "". Always quote expansions; these forms work identically in bash and zsh.
rationale: Mined from orama-system/bin/orama-system/skill/shell-hygiene/SKILL.md §Shell Portability. Bash habits silently break in zsh.

claim: Skill rename/migration pattern: when a skill is renamed (no-sleep-chains -> shell-hygiene, 2026-06-13), the old path becomes a redirect stub that must never be edited for content. Cross-references in sibling repos (AlphaClaw/docs/Lessons.MD) become stale and must be updated to the new canonical path. The canonical target is bin/orama-system/skill/<new-name>/SKILL.md relative to repo root.
rationale: Discovered during progressive disclosure: orama-system/bin/orama-system/skills/no-sleep-chains/SKILL.md is now a redirect stub; AlphaClaw Lessons.md still links to the old path. Pattern applies to all skill renames.

claim: reanchor_scan.sh canonical usage: reanchor_scan.sh <repo_path> [main_ref] [scope] where scope=remotes|heads|all. Builds tree-twin index from origin/main (%T format), walks first-parent history of each ref, finds deepest twin. Output states: MERGED/in-main (tip twin), NEEDS-REANCHOR (graft N commits onto twin), NO-TWIN (shares mb, likely fine), ORPHAN (mb==root). Verifies with: git cherry -v main_ref tip twin_base. This is the ONLY correct branch-state detector after a history rewrite.
rationale: Mined from orama-system/scripts/git/reanchor_scan.sh (75 lines). Canonical method per git-history-surgery SKILL.md §B5. Prevents false behind/ahead conclusions.

Dry-run: --dry-run; CI gate: --check (exits 1 if stale). Surfaces include SKILL.md frontmatter, CLAUDE.md, README badge, agent_registry.json, routing_rules.json, portal_server.py, install.ps1, PERPLEXITY_BRIDGE.md, SYNC_ANALYSIS.md, afrp/README.md, self-discovery/SKILL.md, bin/agents/*/agent.md, bin/mcp_servers/*.py, bin/shared/*.py. claim: Tree-twin re-anchor (correct fix after rewrite): build twin index (git log main --format='%H %T'), find deepest ancestor with same %T. Case A (exact tip twin): push --force-with-lease=old:old origin twin:branch. Case B (no tip twin): git rebase --onto twin base. Verify merge-base HEAD origin/main == twin SHA. Never flatten branches to main; re-anchor moves ref only, does not merge content.
rationale: Mined from orama-system/bin/orama-system/skill/git-history-surgery/references/reanchor-after-rewrite.md (112 lines). Canonical recovery from '600 behind' incident.

claim: When merging branches that both append to .agent memory (lessons.jsonl, episodic/AGENT_LEARNINGS.jsonl), resolve conflicts by UNION — keep both sides, dedup by lesson 'id' (jsonl) or by line (episodic) — then RE-RENDER LESSONS.md from lessons.jsonl via render_lessons.py (never hand-merge the rendered file, AGENTS.md Rule 5). Sanitize any leaked workstation paths first using relative paths or env vars (not <user> placeholders), or pre-commit repo_hygiene (LINT-006) blocks the merge commit. Use a throwaway git worktree to resolve without disturbing main's working tree.
rationale: 2026-06-22: merged origin/main into feat/perpetua-submodule-upgrade for PR #123; 3 .agent files conflicted (both sides appended lessons); union+re-render gave 61 lessons/32 episodic; commit was blocked by /Users/lab and /Users/user leaks in branch dream-cycle content until sanitized.

claim: When the same lessons get duplicated across branches (one bookmarks salvaged content, another syncs the same from upstream), deduplicate to ONE canonical entry: keep the preferred format, GRAFT the other copy's provenance/cross-ref into the survivor (additive — never lose a cross-ref), keep stray lessons grouped + date-ordered.
rationale: 2026-06-22 PR #123: docs/LESSONS.md had the 3 AlphaClaw lessons twice (main bookmarked vs branch synced); kept main's bookmark, grafted provenance, removed dup.

claim: Never put literal workstation paths (/Users/<name>/...) in any tracked file — docs, scripts, memory, or config. Use relative paths (../../, ../filename), env vars ($OPENCLAW_ROOT, $REPO_ROOT), or ~ tilde. LINT-006 in repo_hygiene.py and CIDF Target Verification both enforce this as a pre-commit hard gate. The same rule applies to AI-generated memory content: use relative paths or strip the parent path tree; do NOT use <user> placeholder (it still exposes the directory structure).
rationale: LINT-006 / CIDF anti-doxxing invariant: literal workstation paths in tracked files expose the developer's username and machine layout to anyone with repo access. Caught multiple times (2026-06-22 PR #123 dream-cycle content had /Users/lab and /Users/user). CI and pre-commit both block commits with violations.

claim: Email addresses in ALLOWED_GMAIL_COAUTHORS are NEVER checked for non-gmail domains. The gmail_allowed() gate in check_commit_message.sh only runs when the email ends in @gmail.com or @googlemail.com. Any personal domain (e.g. @cyre.me) stored in ALLOWED_GMAIL_COAUTHORS will silently fall through to DENIED. Fix: put non-gmail personal/org addresses in ALLOWED_EXACT_COAUTHOR_EMAILS instead.
rationale: 2026-06-22: lawrence@cyre.me was in ALLOWED_GMAIL_COAUTHORS; commits with Co-authored-by: cyre <Lawrence@cyre.me> were rejected because gmail_allowed() is guarded by *@gmail.com check. Moved to ALLOWED_EXACT_COAUTHOR_EMAILS (case-insensitive tolower match). Fix in orama scripts/git/check_commit_message.sh, synced to PT via sync-attribution-guard-scripts.sh.

claim: When tracked files contain paths that look absolute (C:\\Users\\..., /Users/...), use relative paths instead (../../, ../) resolved from the file's own location within the repo. Never use username-containing placeholders like <user> or env vars that still expose directory structure (%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\...). The filename alone is sufficient when marked local-only; strip the parent path tree entirely. Standard: relative paths from the file's directory, or ~ for home, or $OPENCLAW_ROOT for the repo root. Applies to all tracked files including .agent/memory JSON and markdown.
rationale: PR #123 2026-06-22: WORKSPACE.md had C:\\Users\\lab\\Downloads\\SKILLS.md\\... — even after replacing with %USERPROFILE%\\Downloads\\..., the subdirectory tree \\Downloads\\SKILLS.md\\ultrathink\\ was still identifying. Correct form: ../Cross-Repo-Memory-Seed.md (relative from working/). Placeholder <user> still reveals path structure.

claim: datetime.fromtimestamp() returns naive local time — always pass tz=datetime.timezone.utc for UTC-aware output. Subtracting a naive datetime from an aware one raises TypeError. Also: datetime.now() without tz= is naive; use datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) everywhere timestamps are compared or stored.
rationale: 2026-06-22 CodeRabbit PR #123: render_lessons.py fromtimestamp without tz= vs fallback datetime.now(utc) produced mixed naive/aware accepted_at; _age_factor subtracted naive now() from possibly UTC-aware staged_at, causing TypeError. Fixed both.

claim: When updating lesson claims in lessons.jsonl, also update the matching sentinel-below bullet in LESSONS.md. Otherwise migrate_legacy_bullets re-reads the old bullet text, finds it absent from existing_claims (since we changed the claim), and re-appends it with the same hash-based ID. _dedupe_by_id keeps the LAST entry per ID, so the re-migrated OLD text wins. Fix: (1) update sentinel bullets to match new claim text, (2) dedup lessons.jsonl keeping FIRST occurrence.
rationale: 2026-06-22 PR #123: updated two lesson claims in lessons.jsonl to fix contradictory guidance; render_lessons re-added old text via migrate_legacy_bullets because sentinel-below LESSONS.md still had old text. Caused duplicate IDs with old text winning.

claim: CodeRabbit reviews every new push to a PR, creating new unresolved threads even after all previous ones were resolved. Always check review thread state after each push, not just once at the start. Merge is only safe when BOTH conditions are true: (a) mergeStateStatus is CLEAN or MERGEABLE, and (b) all review threads are resolved.
rationale: 2026-06-22 PR #123: resolved all 4 CodeRabbit threads in previous session; pushed new commits to fix SAST issues; CodeRabbit created 3 new unresolved threads on the new commit. Merge would have landed with unresolved threads.

claim: When a git pre-push hook runs from a deleted or removed worktree directory (getcwd fails), the hook exits non-zero with 'banned or unapproved attribution in commits to push' — even when NO actual banned pattern exists. The banned_attribution_lib.sh cannot resolve the repo root or patterns file, so it fails closed. The error message is misleading: the real cause is a dead working directory, not a real attribution violation. Fix: never delete a worktree before the git push completes; if a push fails with this message after a worktree cleanup, re-push from a live worktree or the canonical repo directory.
rationale: 2026-06-22: PT #127 branch push blocked with 'banned or unapproved attribution' after the /tmp/rebase-pt127 worktree was removed (git worktree remove --force) before the push command finished. The commits had Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com> which is explicitly allowed (anthropic.com in WELL_KNOWN_COAUTHOR_DOMAIN_SUFFIXES). Confirmed: re-pushing from a fresh worktree with the same commits (after squash) succeeded immediately.
